column1: # Class allow-list for tests/test_g4prose.py (T-74). A token is class-admitted when a row's glob
# matches its file and the row's regex matches a span of the raw line that contains the token.
# Every regex is anchored on a non-numeric marker -- a word, a symbol, a delimiter -- never on the
# digits alone, and every row admits a kind of token that is not a claim about the data: dates,
# citations, identifiers, versions, digests, cross-references. Counts, point numbers, ulp figures,
# rates, percentages, Z and A values, array sizes and coefficients are never admitted here; they
# are pinned or registered. Rows are tried in order; T-75 requires each row's example to match its
# regex and each row to admit at least one live token the rows above it do not.

column4: reason
an ISO calendar date, or a year-month, naming when something was done; not a count
a publication year in parentheses after an author or preprint name, as citations write it
an author-year citation (`Stodden 1990`, `Measday's 2001 review`): the year of a paper, not a quantity
an italicised journal name followed by its year, as the README cites papers

a journal volume, year and page triple that follows a journal name, in either order and with the volume bold or plain, or a page range after `pp.`: a bibliographic locator, quoted from the source that carries it
a DOI, the persistent identifier of a record; its digits are an address, not a value
an ORCID identifier, an address not a value
an arXiv identifier: the submission month and sequence number of a preprint
anything inside a URL, badge links included: path segments, percent-encoded text, DOI and arXiv suffixes are addresses, not statements about the data
a git object name or SHA digest: hexadecimal with at least one letter, the identity of some bytes; the parity tests pin the two the dataset document prints
the Layer-2 bibliography key of the Geant4 release, its tag with dots as underscores; T-55 resolves every shipped bibkey
the `4` of the Geant4 toolkit's name, and of its paths, scripts and environment variables (`geant4-config`, `GEANT4_DATA_DIR`); a brand, not a number
the `G4`/`g4` namespace prefix: Geant4 class and function names, the `G4MUONICDATA` variable, this repository's `g4` package and the `.g4dat` extension
the dataset's name `D1` and the `d1` stem of its files, drivers and reference module: an identifier

a version, release tag or licence version beside the name of the thing it versions (`Geant4 11.4.2`, `v1.2.0`, `Ubuntu 26.04`, `Apache-2.0`), or a Keep a Changelog release heading or link reference (`[1.2.0]`): an identity, not a measurement; the upstream tag is separately pinned by T-40
the interpreter versions the CI matrix names, in the README's `py3.x` form
the compiler identity string as `g++ --version` prints it, recorded verbatim in the oracle header T-48 pins to its producer
the names of architectures, encodings and hash functions that happen to carry digits: `x86_64`, `aarch64`, `arm64`, `binary64`, `IEEE-754`, `SHA-256`, `MD5`
an optimisation level, language-standard flag or standard name (`-O2`, `C++17`): a build setting, not a quantity
the ids of this program's findings (`F-n`), tests (`T-nn`) and C++ checks (`V-nn`): labels
